# ruststream-sqlx

> `ruststream-sqlx` brings SQL databases into RustStream, a Rust framework for services that subscribe to message brokers and publish to them, through `sqlx`: a transactional outbox over any RustStream broker, and task queues in Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB and SQLite tables.

This site holds the entry pages. The crate is documented item by item on docs.rs, and the framework itself on the RustStream site.

## Site

- [Home](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/): the two components and where the rest of the documentation is

## Guides

- [The inbox broker](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#the-inbox-broker): task queues in the service's Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB and SQLite tables, taken by row lock, by lease or by advisory lock; what each handler outcome does to a row, and when to take the inbox or the outbox
- [An event of the service's own](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#an-event-of-the-services-own): `custom(..)` on the derive or `.own::<..>()` by hand, and the event's trait, which run the service's own SQL for one statement of a built-in dialect
- [Macro or manual](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#macro-or-manual): a queue table described by hand, `InboxTable` with the typed builder `InboxSpec`, the one `type Table` line, the role traits, row mode's `Input`, the insert from `dialect::insert`, and where each rule is checked in each form
- [Roles](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#roles): what each `#[field(..)]` role turns on and what a table without it does, with each role's `InboxSpec` setter and trait by hand
- [Time](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#time): "now" from the host's `SystemClock` by default, `clock = DatabaseClock` or a `Clock` of the service's own, the time types `chrono` and `time`, and the real clock in tests
- [Row mode](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#row-mode): a table without a payload column, whose handler takes the row itself, `&Row` or `&[Row]`, with no codec; what settles a row the driver cannot read, and how a row-mode task is written
- [The headers layout](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#the-headers-layout): a queue table described by `#[derive(InboxHeaders)]` and a message struct that flattens it beside data of its own; where the attributes go, the default fetch and its startup check, and the header values `HeaderField` gives
- [A fetch over a join](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#a-fetch-over-a-join): `custom(fetch)` with a `Fetch` that reads the message from other tables, and a claimed id the join finds no row for
- [Row locks, leases or advisory locks](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#row-locks-leases-or-advisory-locks): the three forms a queue table takes its rows in, what each holds while a handler runs, and when to declare `#[field(locked_until)]` or `advisory_lock`
- [The lease form](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#the-lease-form): the claim that commits, the lease as the ownership token, its extension every half lease, `LeaseLost`, and attempts counted at the claim
- [The advisory lock form](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#the-advisory-lock-form): `advisory_lock = ".."` and its key, the claim of candidates, the lock released at settlement, on an unsettled drop and at `shutdown` with its counts, a pool connection per delivery in work, and how Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB and SQLite keep the locks
- [A lock of the service's own](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#a-lock-of-the-services-own): `custom(lock, unlock)` with `Lock` and `Unlock`, and a dialect of the service's own that implements `Advisory`
- [Transactional mode](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#transactional-mode): `.transactional()` at the mount site and `Ctx<keys::Tx<DB>>`, the handler's writes that acknowledgement commits and every other outcome rolls back, what the transaction is in each form, writes through `keys::Pool` that commit on their own, the order of `Ctx` keys, and a pool connection per delivery in work
- [Isolation and mode](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#isolation-and-mode): `isolation = ..` and SQLite's `mode = ..` in `#[inbox(..)]`, which database opens which level, and the compile error for one its dialect does not open
- [FIFO groups](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#fifo-groups): `#[field(group, fifo = true)]`, one row of a group in work, the head in claim order, how retries move it, and a group kept in order by an advisory lock key
- [Databases](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#databases): what Postgres, MySQL 8.0.1 and MariaDB 10.6, SQLite and an `AnyPool` each serve; `SKIP LOCKED` and the oldest servers, `LISTEN/NOTIFY`, `PgBouncer` with advisory locks, isolation in the row lock form, and the indexes a claim needs
- [A dialect of the service's own](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#a-dialect-of-the-services-own): the traits a dialect implements for each form and for subscriptions by name, written from scratch for a database without a built-in dialect
- [Startup checks and rows that do not decode](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#startup-checks-and-rows-that-do-not-decode): what stops a subscription when it opens, and the decode-failure policy that settles a row whose columns do not decode
- [Batches](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#batches): one claim as a batch, settled together in the row lock form and row by row in the lease and advisory lock forms
- [Routes and by-name subscriptions](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#routes-and-by-name-subscriptions): publishing into tables through repositories and routes, `#[subscriber("name")]`, and what each costs per message
- [Waking a subscription](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#waking-a-subscription): the poll interval, and a publish from the same process that wakes the subscriptions of its table and group
- [`LISTEN/NOTIFY` on Postgres](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#listennotify-on-postgres): `listen_notify()`, the channel and payload another writer or a trigger sends, and its cost: a pool connection, a statement per publish, commits that notify one at a time
- [Testing a service on the inbox](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#testing-a-service-on-the-inbox): `TestApp::start_live` against a real database or an in-memory SQLite, the real clock, and the outbox off in test builds unless `RUSTSTREAM_SQLX_OUTBOX=on`
- [The transactional outbox](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#the-transactional-outbox): `#[derive(Outbox)]` or a record described by hand, `outbox!` or `track`, the publish and subscription middlewares, the startup republish, `wrap` for publishes outside handlers, the pool set in `on_startup`, the at-least-once guarantee, the outbox beside the inbox, and the test switch `RUSTSTREAM_SQLX_OUTBOX=on`
